resolution.rationale: The current compiler always rebuilds a one-edge causal_join DIRECTED_PATH goal and the hardened theorem returns the target entity. The actual answer requires route/effect binding, role-anchor matching, passive baseline and source contribution retrieval, CHANGE/STABLE branching, three-channel arithmetic and normalization, and public label lookup. Keeping final RELEASE would therefore misstate what the machine proves; adding A or B would introduce a distinct behavioral or proof-kernel experiment and weaken isolation of the named return edge.

resolution.required_change: Replace the proposal, spec, workflow, scope, graph, loop, visibility matrix, claim, and tests with newly hash-bound option-C bytes. Freeze MEMORY_1 and raw proposal artifacts, then score exact requested-connection closure and attribution strictly offline. The current intake cannot be human-ratified into implementation; it must be superseded by a fresh deliberation and exact human decision.

Because option C needs only a committed closure measurement, online promotion adds causal ambiguity without scientific necessity.

resolution.required_change: Remove online public-evidence admission, support promotion, admission reasons, accept/reject status, and supported-status changes from every dream, selector, memory, realization, checkpoint, thinker, retry, and provider byte in option C.
